Modeling

A multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression model was constructed to evaluate the independent association between baseline risk factors and an incident hypertension event. For the purposes of this study, an outcome event was strictly defined as the first clinical visit during follow-up where a participant exhibited a blood pressure measurement of \(\ge\) 130/80 mmHg or recorded with antihypertensive medication use. The model simultaneously adjusted for age (scaled per 10-year increment), body mass index (BMI) category, and biological sex.

Due to a significant violation of the proportional hazards assumption by the sex variable in preliminary diagnostics, a time-split analysis was implemented. Biological sex was split into two separate observation windows around a 3-year landmark: an early follow-up phase (Years 0–3) and a late follow-up phase (Years after 3).

Overall, no baseline factors demonstrated a statistically significant association with an increased risk of incident hypertension across the follow-up period.
